items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: Tommy threw his trombone at me and I caught it

ctx.x: Well, we had been in there, we're waiting. We had been up all night, and we're in there and they were doing some connecting things, you know, and we're sitting there, and we're waiting for Benny, and we were called at 8:00 o'clock in the morning, and that's makeup at 7:30, and we're waiting and we're waiting and we're waiting, and no Goodman. And finally they call his house. "Well, Mr. Goodman is having breakfast." Well, then, "Mr. Goodman will be there pretty soon." Well, to make a long story short, Benny

comes walking in around 11:30. By now, Tommy's fuse is lit. He's so mad he cannot be contained, you know, and one word led to another and we started in, you know. And we played it, it was a thing in unison, and we finished the thing. Little rings, we were doing. And Benny just kept on playing, like that, so Tommy said, "All right, Benny. We all know how good you play. Now come on, let's do this and get out of here. We've been here all morning." And one word led to another. Tommy threw his trombone at me and I…

Another thing that happened there, Louis Armstrong, you know, always played a little bit sharp. I mean all musicians know that. So this thing was in unison that we were playing. So Emil Newman, who was the musical director for this thing, he said, "Look, you get Pops aside and talk to him." So I got Pops over and I'm talking to him, and I see Emil go over and he gets the trumpet and he pulls the slide out about an inch, or an inch and a half or something. Now, he comes over and he says, "Okay." So we come back and
